[FACT] Session Date: 2023/05/28 (Sun) 15:16  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User research plays a crucial role in product development.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User research helps to explain user behavior by observing how users interact with a product or service.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User research helps to gain a deeper understanding of user needs and preferences by gathering feedback and data.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User research helps to identify pain points, difficulties, and barriers that users face when using a product.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User research helps to understand how customers feel about a solution, product, feature, etc., by conducting surveys or user interviews.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Businesses can select target customer segments that are most likely to benefit from the product.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Businesses can understand the user's choice of problem to solve, which informs product development.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Businesses can develop appropriate pricing strategies, reach channels, messages, etc., to effectively market the product.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Businesses can make informed choices about which features to develop and how to design the product's user interface and user experience.  
[USER] Rephrase: Understand the user's choice of problem to solve, which informs product development.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gaining an understanding of the user's preferred problem to solve can provide crucial insights that inform the product development process.  
[USER] When to conduct User interview and when to conduct Survey? Compare.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User interviews are best conducted when a deeper understanding of user needs and behaviors is required.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User interviews are more conversational in nature, allowing for follow-up questions and a greater exploration of topics.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User interviews can help to uncover unmet needs, pain points, and other barriers to product adoption.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User interviews are typically conducted with a smaller sample size, often in-person or over the phone, and are more time-consuming and resource-intensive than surveys.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Surveys are best suited for collecting quantitative data from a larger sample size.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Surveys can provide a snapshot of user preferences and behaviors at a specific point in time and are more efficient than user interviews.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Surveys can be administered online or in-person, and often include closed-ended questions that can be easily analyzed for trends and patterns.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Surveys may not capture the depth of insight that can be gained from user interviews and may not be as effective at uncovering new or unexpected user needs or pain points.
